stages.title: JAINISM: CORE DISTINCTIONS
stages.terms: A high-scoring opening states that Jainism is pluralistic realism with non-absolutist finite predication and a material theory of karmic bondage.
stages.mechanism: It also differs from Nyāya, where the self is conscious through conjunction with mind; in Jainism consciousness belongs intrinsically to jīva.
stages.consequence: Distinction. ✅ The Tīrthaṅkaras are liberated teachers and ford-makers, not creator Gods; Jainism remains anīśvaravāda (non-theistic about creation).
stages.trap: Distinction. ✅ Jainism is pluralistic: there are many jīvas, not one universal self.
stages.answer: Jainism (Jina-centred path of many-sided reality and liberation) is a pluralist realism in which anekāntavāda (doctrine of many-sided reality) holds that enduring dravya (substance) possesses guṇa (qualities) and changing paryāya (modes).
